headline: Oil Prices Slump as US Election Results Ease Middle East Conflict Risks
summary: Brent crude prices have fallen approximately 20% this week to around $95 per barrel, marking the largest weekly decline since the pandemic. The drop follows US midterm election results that reduced concerns over potential escalation of Middle East conflicts.
why: Oil prices are highly sensitive to geopolitical risk premiums. A perceived reduction in conflict risk in the Middle East often leads to a rapid unwinding of these premiums in global energy markets.
why_moved: The market reacted to the US election outcome by pricing in a lower probability of military escalation in the Middle East, causing a sharp sell-off in oil futures.
